agent-orchestration-master

Design agent roles, delegation, handoffs, and shared work around the actual task.

This Skill helps choose whether delegation adds a distinct contribution, map work to the host's actual roles and carriers, coordinate dependencies and mutable targets, and preserve accountable handoffs. It treats a single agent as sufficient by default when no real coordination need exists.

Use and dependencies

Provide the complete agent-orchestration-master/ directory through your assistant's Skill mechanism when designing or operating multi-agent work. The paired prompt-audit-orchestration package uses this Skill for its agent roles and handoffs; this Skill does not own that audit's domain routing or repair authority.

The conditional companion Skills multi-agent-patterns (topology design), harness-engineering (durable agent Harnesses), and tool-design (tool interfaces) are not included in this collection yet. project-development, cloud-local-workflow, and model-conversation-relay may be useful for the specific work they own; they are not required for ordinary delegation. Follow the current host's model policy and actual agent catalog; no model version is prescribed here.

Host-native role support, isolation, and delegation interfaces are runtime capabilities, not Skill dependencies. Inspect them before dispatch and report unsupported mappings instead of assuming role-name compatibility.

Independence and license

The package adapts a local method into a host-neutral workflow. It removes host-specific agent formats and publication commands while retaining role scope, task ownership, dispatch context, safe parallelism, review selection, integration, and native-carrier readback.

This package uses the MIT License. Obtain the complete directory from GitHub.
